newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks to clear up public company debts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks to clear up public company debts.

text.p: The Brazilian government published a decree Wednesday allowing state-owned holdings to pay off debts to the government with untradeable, securitized debt paper received as payment for privatized subsidiaries.
The decree says the paper may be used for payment of debts which came overdue before December 31, 1992, and, when authorized by the government, for more recent debt.
Any leftover debt paper may be transformed into P-Series National Treasury Letters, known as NTN-Ps, or other letters of credit backed by the Treasury.

The decree seeks to clear up the finances of public sector holdings, in particular Eletrobras and Petrobras, which received untradeable public debt in partial compensation for the privatization of subsidiaries.
"The idea is to promote a clear-up of debt within the public sector," an official at the National Treasury said.
